test_assurance_observations.title: Optional Anvil availability check treats bare command names as installed
test_assurance_observations.observation: The documented optional skip path uses available = (!ANVIL.includes('/') || existsSync(ANVIL)) && existsSync(SOLC) && existsSync(REF). A bare name such as the default anvil passes this check regardless of whether it resolves on PATH. With solc and the reference source present but no Anvil binary, the suite is selected and startup rejects through the spawn error handler instead of skipping. REQUIRE_ANVIL is not needed for that path.
test_assurance_observations.defensive_implication: Optional local qualification can fail for a missing optional dependency even though the source documents a skip. This is a test harness issue, not an application defect or a claim about this environment.
test_assurance_observations.remediation: Resolve a bare executable name against PATH, or use an explicit capability check before selecting the suite; keep REQUIRE_ANVIL as the explicit fail-if-missing gate. Preserve clear distinction between skipped and executed integration coverage.

test_assurance_observations.title: Final RegistryView negative case does not isolate malformed registry-entry handling
test_assurance_observations.observation: The case titled reports no entry, bad input and malformed entries configures only an empty bytes entry, checks the no-entry message, then enters a syntactically valid ENS name and checks for any alert. It never supplies malformed registry-entry bytes for a valid address. Those assertions therefore do not independently establish the malformed-entry UI path described by the title.
test_assurance_observations.defensive_implication: A route-level malformed-entry regression could remain untested by this case. This is not a claim that malformed registry values are accepted or that the whole repository lacks coverage: registry.anvil.test.ts lines 141-145 separately assert adapter rejection of malformed stored bytes.
test_assurance_observations.remediation: Split the route cases and supply a malformed registry result after a valid deployment/typehash response for a valid address; assert the intended refusal and absence of usable lookup data. Narrow the current title to its actual assertions if no additional route case is intended.

Real-camera-wrapper tests with fake MediaDevices observe live track counts and cancelled late-stream identity; multipart tests retain the real assembler; visibility tests explicitly refuse hidden dispatch before visibilitychange delivery and after synchronous preview invalidation.

All seven registry test/support versions read, including the reference ERC-1271 fixture and the optional Anvil test source. Assertions cover public-link consent, backup gates, exact reviewed registration/clear call data, strict registry identity checks, delayed consent withdrawal, ENS input invalidation and network-authority revocation. The local blockchain harness was not started.

Common and clipboard tests assert opt-in timers, invalid-delay refusal, matching-content double-read checks, superseded copy generations, permission failures, truthful stale-copy UI state, delayed object-URL revocation and cleanup on browser exceptions. These assertions do not establish atomic clipboard compare-and-clear or real-browser permissions.
